feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 1 (the only raced design with the seven-sensor array) raced zero finishes. Its line_loss_events were 2 on the oval and 1 on the S-bend and slalom, max_error was 0.064 to 0.068 m, and steering_oscillation rose to 0.186 from 0.075 in iteration 0 when kp went from 2.5 to 3.0. The Integrator therefore lowers kp to 2.5 and raises kd to 0.20 to damp the oscillation, and lowers base_speed to 1.3 so the robot can correct on bends. The 12 mm footprint is the common factor in the line-loss events, since a 12 mm sensor sees tape only to about 18.5 mm offset, and that is why 16 mm is the requested change. Decide the next geometry from what the next race shows. If line_loss_events is still above zero on the oval or S-bend with 16 mm footprints, widen the span or move y forward before changing mass, because the footprint alone did not close the gap. If line_loss_events is zero but max_error still approaches 0.06 m, reduce mass to 0.6 kg rather than changing body_width, because body_width cannot move the off-track limit above 0.06 m. If runs complete but completion_time exceeds 2.5 s, test wheel_radius 0.035 m for more top speed, since the lower base_speed may be slowing the robot.
requested_changes: Keep sensor_size at 0.016 m with the seven sensors at x = -0.03 to +0.03 m and y = 0.04 m. If line_loss_events stays above zero on the oval or S-bend, move the sensors forward to y = 0.06 m or widen the span, since iteration 1 showed a 12 mm footprint loses the tape at offsets of about 0.019 m and above.

If max_error still approaches 0.06 m with line_loss_events at zero, reduce mass to 0.6 kg, because iteration 1 showed max_error of 0.068 m from controller lag and body_width cannot raise the 0.06 m off-track limit.
If runs complete but completion_time exceeds 2.5 s, test wheel_radius 0.035 m, because the Integrator lowered base_speed to 1.3 and top speed now limits the finish time.
